clinician.final_diagnosis: Stanford Type A aortic dissection extending from the aortic root to the aortic bifurcation
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 69-year-old woman with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and family history of aortic aneurysms presented to the ED with abrupt onset abdominal pain radiating to her back and chest, initially misattributed to irritable bowel syndrome due to prior history and tenesmus. Physical examination revealed only diffuse abdominal tenderness without pulse discrepancies. Imaging confirmed Stanford Type A aortic dissection extending from the aortic root to the bifurcation. She underwent medical optimization with nicardipine and esmolol infusions for blood pressure and heart rate control, Cardiothoracic Surgery consultation, and emergent operative intervention. She experienced complete recovery during an 8-day hospitalization and was discharged.
